speaker: Doctor
text: There seems to be a discrepancy; the symptoms you described—a fever, rash, headache, and rhinorrhea—are not consistent with Pyelonephritis, which is a kidney infection. Did you perhaps have a fever or pain in your back or sides recently, or is there any confusion about the nature of the rash?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). The combination of a pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and a facial rash that spares the perioral area is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection. The normal white blood cell count further supports a viral etiology rather than a bacterial infection.
